Because that's the disease. That's like the specific definition of the disease. XD
The principal, defining symptom of schizophrenia is an inability to correctly distinguish fantasy from reality. That's precisely what "believing in a delusion" is.

Not a schizophrenic, but I have had my share of hallucinations (chronic sleep deprivation is bad news bears). When your mind receives conflicting sensory input, you try to determine what is real and what is not. The longer this goes on, the harder it becomes due to emotional and psychological fatigue. E.g. hallucinating a life-sized Michelin Man sitting on the hood of your car or the road transmogrifying into Minas Morgul when you're barreling along at 130km/h is disconcerting, but it's /transitory/. You'll snap out of it in 30 seconds or so one way or another. The challenge that skizophrenics face, particularly paranoid skizophrenics, is that the hallucinations can go on for /days/. Seeing a bengal tiger prowling down the hall at night is frightening, even when it fades in under a minute. Skizophrenic episodes can go on much, much longer - and for bonus suffering, a lot of medication for that mental illness is substantially hampered by alcohol, which a lot or people use as a go-to for handling psychological trauma and fear.
